attempts.summary: Deployed a Python HTTP app on node2's private-network interface (10.50.50.11:8080, isolated to a dedicated firewalld zone bound to enp8s0). Configured VyOS on node1 as the WireGuard server (wg0 10.200.0.1/24, UDP 51820) terminating the tunnel, forwarding traffic from wg0 to the private eth1 network (10.50.50.0/24) shared only with node2, with default-drop input/forward firewall filters. Configured node3 (outside the private network) as a WireGuard client (wg0 10.200.0.2/24) routing 10.50.50.0/24 over the tunnel; added a return static route on node2 for 10.200.0.0/24 via node1. Falsified the tunnel dependency by stopping wg-quick on node3 and showing the app becomes unreachable (route falls back to the public LAN, no path to 10.50.50.0/24), then restored it and re-confirmed access. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (VyOS `reboot`, RHEL `systemctl reboot`) using the acknowledge-then-disconnect pattern; boot_id changes were captured for each, and full recovery (WireGuard interfaces/peers, private IPs, static route, firewalld zone, app service, and end-to-end curl through the tunnel) was verified after each restart.
